## QUESTION

1. __Take time to get to know your data.__ Based on some initial exploration, identify 3 variables in the dataset you think will have strong predictive ability for determining if a house was built before 1980. Explain/justify the reasoning behind your guesses (for example with plots).

_The bar graph shows the distribution of houses built before 1980 versus those built during or after 1980, based on the `finbsmnt` (finished basement area) variable. The mjaority of them have an area of 0, indicating that many houses built before 1980 did not have finished basements. After 1980, the area never exceeds 2000._

```{python}
# Additional imports
from lets_plot import *
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

df = df.with_columns(
    (pl.col("yrbuilt") < 1980).alias("before_1980")
)

print(df.describe())

numeric_cols = [c for c, d in zip(df.columns, df.dtypes)
                if d in [pl.Int64, pl.Float64, pl.Int32, pl.Float32]
                and c != "yrbuilt"]

corrs = []

for col in numeric_cols:
    try:
        corr = (
            df.select(
                pl.corr(pl.col(col), pl.col("yrbuilt"))
            ).item()
        )
        corrs.append((col, abs(corr)))
    except:
        pass

corr_df = (
    pl.DataFrame(corrs, schema=["variable", "abs_corr"])
    .sort("abs_corr", descending=True)
)

print(corr_df.head(10))

ggplot(df, aes("livearea", fill="before_1980")) + \
    geom_histogram(alpha=.6, bins=30)

ggplot(df, aes("numbaths", fill="before_1980")) + \
    geom_histogram(alpha=.6, bins=20)

ggplot(df, aes("finbsmnt", fill="before_1980")) + \
    geom_histogram(alpha=.6, bins=30)
```

2. __Build a classification model labeling houses as being built “before 1980” or “during or after 1980”.__ Your goal is to reach or exceed 90% accuracy. Report your final model choice and any other model parameters you may have tweaked (train-test split ratio, tuning parameters, etc).  

_While this didn't exceed 90% accuracy, it provides a good starting point for further improvement._

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
# Don't forget, you need another import statement to import the desired ML model from sklearn
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

df = df.with_columns(
    (pl.col("yrbuilt") < 1980).alias("before_1980")
)

predictors = [
    "livearea",
    "finbsmnt",
    "basement",
    "stories",
    "nocars",
    "numbdrm",
    "numbaths",
    "sprice",
    "netprice",
    "tasp"
]

X = df.select(predictors).to_numpy()
y = df["before_1980"].cast(pl.Int8).to_numpy()

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X,
    y,
    test_size=0.20,
    random_state=42,
    stratify=y
)

rf = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=300,
    max_depth=12,
    min_samples_leaf=3,
    random_state=42
)

rf.fit(X_train, y_train)

pred = rf.predict(X_test)

accuracy = metrics.accuracy_score(y_test, pred)

print(f"Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f}")
print(metrics.confusion_matrix(y_test, pred))
print(metrics.classification_report(y_test, pred))

```
